context.title: The Final Six Lots
context.summary: The remaining tribes receive their land: Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali and Dan. Last of all, Joshua receives his own town, Timnath-serah.
context.background: Simeon's towns lie inside Judah because Judah's share was too large (v. 9), fitting Jacob's words that Simeon would be scattered in Israel (Genesis 49:7). Zebulun, Issachar, Asher and Naphtali settled in the north, around the Jezreel Valley and Galilee. Dan found its land too small and later captured Leshem (Laish) in the far north, a story told in Judges 18.
watchFor: Dan's territory 'went out too little for them' (v. 47).
Joshua, the leader, takes his own inheritance last (vv. 49–50).
A formal closing to the whole division of land (v. 51).

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Simeon
people.summary: The second son of Jacob by Leah (Gen. 29:33). He was associated with Levi in the terrible act of vengeance against Hamor and the Shechemites (34:25, 26).

people.name: Zebulun
people.summary: Dwelling, the sixth and youngest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 30:20). Little is known of his personal history.

people.name: Issachar
people.summary: Hired (Gen. 30:18). “God hath given me,” said Leah, “my hire (Heb. sekhari)...and she called his name Issachar.” He was Jacob’s ninth son, and was born in Padan-aram (comp. 28:2).

people.name: Asher
people.summary: Happy, Jacob’s eigth son; his mother was Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid (Gen. 30:13). Of the tribe founded by him nothing is recorded beyond its holding a place in the list of the tribes (35:26; 46:17; Ex. 1:4, etc.) It increased in numbers twenty-nine percent, during the thirty-eight years’ wanderings.

people.name: Naphtali
people.summary: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid (Gen. 30:8). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons (Gen. 46:24).

people.name: Allon
people.summary: The son of Jedaiah, of the family of the Simeonites, who expelled the Hamites from the valley of Gedor (1 Chr. 4:37).

people.name: Dan
people.summary: The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Joshua
people.summary: Jehovah is his help, or Jehovah the Saviour. The son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, the successor of Moses as the leader of Israel.

people.name: Nun
people.summary: Beyond the fact that he was the father of Joshua nothing more is known of him (Ex. 33:11).

people.name: Eleazar
people.summary: The third son of Aaron (Ex. 6:23). His wife, a daughter of Putiel, bore him Phinehas (Ex. 6:25). After the death of Nadab and Abihu (Lev. 10:12; Num. 3:4) he was appointed to the charge of the sanctuary (Num. 3:32).

places.name: Beersheba
places.summary: Well of the oath, or well of seven, a well dug by Abraham, and so named because he and Abimelech here entered into a compact (Gen. 21:31). On re-opening it, Isaac gave it the same name (Gen. 26:31-33).

places.name: Moladah
places.summary: Birth, a city in the south of Judah which fell to Simeon (Josh. 15:21-26; 19:2).

places.name: Sheba
places.summary: Heb. id. A kingdom in Arabia Felix. Sheba, in fact, was Saba in Southern Arabia, the Sabaeans of classical geography, who carried on the trade in spices with the other peoples of the ancient world.

places.name: Balah
places.summary: A city in the tribe of Simeon (Josh. 19:3), elsewhere called Bilhah (1 Chr. 4:29) and Baalah (Josh. 15:29).

places.name: Hazar-shual
places.summary: Village or enclosure of the jackal, a city on the south border of Judah (Josh. 15:28; Neh. 11:27).

places.name: Hormah
places.summary: Banning; i.e., placing under a “ban,” or devoting to utter destruction. After the manifestation of God’s anger against the Israelites, on account of their rebellion and their murmurings when the spies returned to the camp at Kadesh, in the wilderness of Paran, with an evil report of the land, they quickly repented of their conduct, and presumed to go up “to the head of the mountain,” seeking to enter the Promised Land, but without the presence of the Lord, without the ark of…

places.name: Hazar-susah
places.summary: Village of the horse, the same as Sansannah, one of Solomon’s “chariot cities” (Josh. 15:31; 2 Chr. 1:14), a depot in the south border of Judah.

places.name: Ziklag
places.summary: A town in the Negeb, or south country of Judah (Josh. 15:31), in the possession of the Philistines when David fled to Gath from Ziph with all his followers.

places.name: Sharuhen
places.summary: now Tel Sharuhen

places.name: Rimmon
places.summary: One of the “uttermost cities” of Judah, afterwards given to Simeon (Josh. 15:21, 32; 19:7; 1 Chr. 4:32). In Josh. 15:32 Ain and Rimmon are mentioned separately, but in 19:7 and 1 Chr. 4:32 (comp. Neh. 11:29) the two words are probably to be combined, as forming together the name of one place, Ain-Rimmon=the spring of the pomegranate.

places.name: Baalath-beer
places.summary: Baalah of the well, (Josh. 19:8, probably the same as Baal, mentioned in 1 Chr. 4:33, a city of Simeon.

places.name: Negeb
places.summary: Heb. Negeb, that arid district to the south of Palestine through which lay the caravan route from Central Palestine to Egypt (Gen. 12:9; 13:1, 3; 46:1-6).

places.name: Ramah
places.summary: A city first mentioned in Josh. 18:25, near Gibeah of Benjamin. It was fortified by Baasha, king of Israel (1 Kings 15:17-22; 2 Chr. 16:1-6).

places.name: Zebulun
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1266 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Jokneam
places.summary: Gathered by the people, (Josh. 19:11; 21:34), a city “of Carmel” (12:22), i.e., on Carmel, allotted with its suburbs to the Merarite Levites.

places.name: Mareal
places.summary: Trembling, a place on the southern boundary of Zebulun (Josh. 19:11).

places.name: Daberath
places.summary: Pasture, a Levitical town of Issachar (Josh. 19:12; 21:28), near the border of Zebulum. It is the modern small village of Deburich, at the base of Mount Tabor.

places.name: Japhia
places.summary: A town in the southern boundary of Zebulum (Josh. 19:12); now Yafa, 2 miles south-west of Nazareth.

places.name: Gath-hepher
places.summary: Wine-press of the well, a town of Lower Galilee, about 5 miles from Nazareth; the birthplace of Jonah (2 Kings 14:25); the same as Gittah-hepher (Josh. 19:13).

places.name: Neah
places.summary: Shaking, or settlement, or descent, a town on the east side of Zebulun, not far from Rimmon (Josh. 19:13).

places.name: Bethlehem
places.summary: A city of Zebulun, mentioned only in Josh. 19:15.

places.name: Idalah
places.summary: Snares(?), a city near the west border of Zebulun (Josh. 19:15).

places.name: Kattath
places.summary: (Josh. 19:15), a town of Asher, has been identified with Kana el Jelil.

places.name: Nahalal
places.summary: Pasture, a city in Zebulun on the border of Issachar (Josh. 19:15), the same as Nahalol (Judg. 1:30). It was given to the Levites.

places.name: Shimron
places.summary: Watch-post, an ancient city of the Canaanites; with its villages, allotted to Zebulun (Josh. 19:15); now probably Semunieh, on the northern edge of the plain of Esdraelon, 5 miles west of Nazareth.

places.name: Issachar
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1265 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Chesulloth
places.summary: Fertile places; the loins, a town of Issachar, on the slopes of some mountain between Jezreel and Shunem (Josh. 19:18).

places.name: Jezreel
places.summary: A town of Issachar (Josh. 19:18), where the kings of Israel often resided (1 Kings 18:45; 21:1; 2 Kings 9:30). Here Elijah met Ahab, Jehu, and Bidkar; and here Jehu executed his dreadful commission against the house of Ahab (2 Kings 9:14-37; 10:1-11).

places.name: Shunem
places.summary: Two resting-places, a little village in the tribe of Issachar, to the north of Jezreel and south of Mount Gilboa (Josh. 19:18), where the Philistines encamped when they came against Saul (1 Sam. 28:4), and where Elisha was hospitably entertained by a rich woman of the place.

places.name: Shion
places.summary: Overturning, a town of Issachar (Josh. 19:19).

places.name: Ebez
places.summary: Tin, or white, a town in the tribe of Issachar (Josh. 19:20), at the north of the plain of Esdraelon.

places.name: Kishion
places.summary: Hardness, a city of Issachar assigned to the Gershonite Levites (Josh. 19:20), the same as Kishon (21:28).

places.name: En-gannim
places.summary: A city on the border of Machar (Josh. 19:21), allotted to the Gershonite Levites (21:29). It is identified with the modern Jenin, a large and prosperous town of about 4,000 inhabitants, situated 15 miles south of Mount Tabor, through which the road from Jezreel to Samaria and Jerusalem passes.

places.name: Remeth
places.summary: Another form of Ramah or Ramoth (1 Chr. 6:73; Josh. 19:21), and probably also of Jarmuth (Josh. 21:29).

places.name: Beth-shemesh
places.summary: A city between Dothan and the Jordan, near the southern border of Issachar (Josh. 19:22), 7 1/2 miles south of Beth-shean.

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: But besides these two historical fountains there is a third, called the Hasbany, which rises in the bottom of a valley at the western base of Hermon, 12 miles north of Tell-el-Kady.

places.name: Tabor
places.summary: Now Jebel et-Tur, a cone-like prominent mountain, 11 miles west of the Sea of Galilee. It is about 1,843 feet high. The view from the summit of it is said to be singularly extensive and grand.

places.name: Asher
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1264 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Achshaph
places.summary: Fascination, a royal city of the Canaanites, in the north of Palestine (Josh. 11:1; 12:20; 19:25).

places.name: Helkath
places.summary: Smoothness, a town of Asher, on the east border (Josh. 19:25; 21:31); called also Hukok (1 Chr. 6:75).

places.name: Carmel
places.summary: A town in the hill country of Judah (Josh. 15:55), the residence of Nabal (1 Sam. 25:2, 5, 7, 40), and the native place of Abigail, who became David’s wife (1 Sam. 27:3).

places.name: Mishal
places.summary: A city of the tribe of Asher (Josh. 21:30; 1 Chr. 6:74).

places.name: Shihor-libnath
places.summary: Black-white, a stream on the borders of Asher, probably the modern Nahr Zerka, i.e., the “crocodile brook,” or “blue river”, which rises in the Carmel range and enters the Mediterranean a little to the north of Caesarea (Josh. 19:26).

places.name: Beth-dagon
places.summary: A city near the south-east border of Asher (Josh. 19:27). It was a Philistine colony.

places.name: Cabul
places.summary: A town on the eastern border of Asher (Josh. 19:27), probably one of the towns given by Solomon to Hiram; the modern Kabul, some 8 miles east of Accho, on the very borders of Galilee.

places.name: Neiel
places.summary: Dwelling-place of God, a town in the territory of Asher, near its southern border (Josh. 19:27).

places.name: Ebron
places.summary: A town in the north border of Asher (Josh. 19:28).

places.name: Hammon
places.summary: A town in the tribe of Asher, near Zidon (Josh. 19:28), identified with ‘Ain Hamul.

places.name: Kanah
places.summary: A town in the north of Asher (Josh. 19:28). It has been identified with ‘Ain-Kana, a village on the brow of a valley some 7 miles south-east of Tyre.

places.name: Rehob
places.summary: A town of Asher (Josh. 19:28), to the east of Zidon.

places.name: Achzib
places.summary: A Phoenician city (the Gr. Ecdippa), always retained in their possession though assigned to the tribe of Asher (Josh. 19:29; Judg. 1:31).

places.name: Hosah
places.summary: A place on the border of the tribe of Asher (Josh. 19:29), a little to the south of Zidon.

places.name: Ramah
places.summary: A town identified with Rameh, on the border of Asher, about 13 miles south-east of Tyre, “on a solitary hill in the midst of a basin of green fields” (Josh. 19:29).

places.name: Tyre
places.summary: A rock, now es-Sur; an ancient Phoenician city, about 23 miles, in a direct line, north of Acre, and 20 south of Sidon. Sidon was the oldest Phoenician city, but Tyre had a longer and more illustrious history.

places.name: Aphek
places.summary: A city of the tribe of Asher. It was the scene of the licentious worship of the Syrian Aphrodite.

places.name: Rehob
places.summary: Another town of Asher (Josh. 19:30), kept possession of by the Canaanites (Judg. 1:31).

places.name: Ummah
places.summary: Vicinity, a town of Asher (Josh. 19:30).

places.name: Naphtali
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1260 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Adami-nekeb
places.summary: Cavern, a town on the boundary of Naphtali (Josh. 19:33).

places.name: Heleph
places.summary: Exchange, a city on the north border of Naphtali (Josh. 19:33).

places.name: Jabneel
places.summary: A town on the border of Naphtali (Josh. 19:33).

places.name: Zaanannim
places.summary: Wanderings; the unloading of tents, so called probably from the fact of nomads in tents encamping amid the cities and villages of that region, a place in the north-west of Lake Merom, near Kedesh, in Naphtali.

places.name: Hukkok
places.summary: Decreed, a town near Zebulun, not far from Jordan, on the border of Naphtali (Josh. 19:34).

places.name: Chinnereth
places.summary: Lyre, the singular form of the word (Deut. 3:17; Josh. 19:35), which is also used in the plural form, Chinneroth, the name of a fenced city which stood near the shore of the lake of Galilee, a little to the south of Tiberias.

places.name: Hammath
places.summary: Warm springs, one of the “fenced cities” of Naphtali (Josh. 19:35).

places.name: Rakkath
places.summary: Shore-town, a “fenced city” of the tribe of Naphtali (Josh. 19:35).

places.name: Ziddim
places.summary: Sides, a town of Naphtali (Josh. 19:35), has been identified with Kefr-Hattin, the “village of the Hittites,” about 5 miles west of Tiberias.

places.name: Adamah
places.summary: Red earth, a fortified city of Naphtali, probably the modern Damieh, on the west side of the sea of Tiberias (Josh. 19:33, 36).

places.name: Hazor
places.summary: A stronghold of the Canaanites in the mountains north of Lake Merom (Josh. 11:1-5). Jabin the king with his allied tribes here encountered Joshua in a great battle.

places.name: Ramah
places.summary: One of the “fenced cities” of Naphtali (Josh. 19:36), on a mountain slope, about seven and a half miles west-south-west of Safed, and 15 miles west of the north end of the Sea of Galilee, the present large and well-built village of Rameh.

places.name: Edrei
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1261 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Edrei
places.summary: One of the chief towns of the kingdom of Bashan (Josh. 12:4, 5). Here Og was defeated by the Israelites, and the strength of the Amorites broken (Num. 21:33-35).

places.name: Kedesh
places.summary: A “fenced city” of Naphtali, one of the cities of refuge (Josh. 19:37; Judg. 4:6). It was assigned to the Gershonite Levites (Josh. 21:32). It was originally a Canaanite royal city (Josh. 12:22), and was the residence of Barak (Judg. 4:6); and here he and Deborah assembled the tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali before the commencement of the conflict with Sisera in the plain of Esdraelon, “for Jehovah among the mighty” (9, 10).

places.name: Beth-anath
places.summary: House of response, one of the fenced cities of Naphtali (Josh. 19:38).

places.name: Beth-shemesh
places.summary: One of the fenced cities of Naphtali (Josh. 19:38), between Mount Tabor and the Jordan. Now Khurbet Shema, 3 miles west of Safed.

places.name: Horem
places.summary: Consecrated, one of the fenced cities of Naphtali (Josh. 19:38).

places.name: Migdal-el
places.summary: Tower of God, a fortified city of Naphtali (Josh. 19:38), supposed by some to be identical with Magdala.

places.name: Yiron
places.summary: now Yaroun

places.name: Dan
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1259 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Eshtaol
places.summary: Narrow pass or recess, a town (Josh. 15:33) in the low country, the She-phelah of Judah. It was allotted to the tribe of Dan (Josh. 19:41), and was one of their strongholds.

places.name: Zorah
places.summary: Place of wasps, a town in the low country of Judah, afterwards given to Dan (Josh. 19:41; Judg. 18:2), probably the same as Zoreah (Josh. 15:33).

places.name: Aijalon
places.summary: A city in the tribe of Zebulun (Judg. 12:12), the modern Jalun, three miles north of Cabul.

places.name: Ithlah
places.summary: Suspended; high, a city on the borders of Dan (Josh. 19:42).

places.name: Shaalabbin
places.summary: Or Shaal’bim, a place of foxes, a town of the tribe of Dan (Josh. 19:42; Judg. 1:35). It was one of the chief towns from which Solomon drew his supplies (1 Kings 4:9).

places.name: Ekron
places.summary: Firm-rooted, the most northerly of the five towns belonging to the lords of the Philistines, about 11 miles north of Gath. It was assigned to Judah (Josh. 13:3), and afterwards to Dan (19:43), but came again into the full possession of the Philistines (1 Sam. 5:10).

places.name: Baalath
places.summary: A town of the tribe of Dan (Josh. 19:44). It was fortified by Solomon (1 Kings 9:18; 2 Chr. 8:6).

places.name: Eltekeh
places.summary: God is its fear, a city in the tribe of Dan. It was a city of refuge and a Levitical city (Josh. 21:23).

places.name: Gibbethon
places.summary: A height, a city of the Philistines in the territory of Dan, given to the Kohathites (Josh. 19:44; 21:23). Nadab the king of Israel, while besieging it, was slain under its walls by Baasha, one of his own officers (1 Kings 15:27).

places.name: Bene-berak
places.summary: uk.geocities.com/jonpartin/joshua4.html

places.name: Gath-rimmon
places.summary: A Levitical city in the tribe of Dan (Josh. 19:45; 21:24; 1 Chr. 6:69).

places.name: Jehud
places.summary: now Yehud

places.name: Joppa
places.summary: Beauty, a town in the portion of Dan (Josh. 19:46; A.V., “Japho”), on a sandy promontory between Caesarea and Gaza, and at a distance of 30 miles north-west from Jerusalem.

places.name: Me-jarkon
places.summary: Waters of yellowness, or clear waters, a river in the tribe of Dan (Josh. 19:46).

places.name: Rakkon
places.summary: A place upon the shore, a town belonging to Dan (Josh. 19:46).

places.name: Dan
places.summary: The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni).

places.name: Ephraim (Territory)
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1270 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Timnath-serah
places.summary: Remaining portion, the city of Joshua in the hill country of Ephraim, the same as Timnath-heres (Josh. 19:50; 24:30). “Of all sites I have seen,” says Lieut.

places.name: Shiloh
places.summary: Generally understood as denoting the Messiah, “the peaceful one,” as the word signifies (Gen. 49:10). The Vulgate Version translates the word, “he who is to be sent,” in allusion to the Messiah; the Revised Version, margin, “till he come to Shiloh;” and the LXX., “until that which is his shall come to Shiloh.”
